result.title: SurgStream: A Workflow-Anchored Proactive Streaming Framework and Benchmark for Real-Time Surgical Video Understanding
result.summary: Surgical video understanding is essential for intraoperative assistance such as workflow monitoring, instrument preparation and procedural documentation. Delivering such assistance in real time requires a model to jointly perceive the ongoing scene, remember past surgical events, and respond before clinically relevant moments pass. Existing approaches provide limited support for jointly retaining procedural evidence and deciding when to respond in streaming surgical video. In this work, we propose SurgStream, a workflow-anchored proactive streaming framework for real-time surgical video understanding. We first introduce Workflow-Anchored Memory (WAM) to record structured instrument-action-target observations and fold them into phase-level summaries, providing compact and queryable surgical memory. Deadline-aware Transition Learning (DTL) is then devised to supervise response states within clinical windows, enabling timely responses before procedural deadlines. We further introduce SurgStream-Bench, comprising 11.7K streaming interactions across various tasks covering real-time perception, backward memory queries, forward proactive QA, proactive alerts and caption memory. Experiments on SurgStream-Bench show gains over state-of-the-art methods, especially in memory and forward proactive QA. The source code will be available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SurgStream：面向实时手术视频的流程锚定主动式流式理解框架，包含记录器械—动作—目标观测并折叠为阶段摘要的 Workflow-Anchored Memory、在临床时间窗内监督响应状态的 Deadline-aware Transition Learning，以及含 11.7K 交互的 SurgStream-Bench 基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时响应」的截止时间窗监督与阶段级记忆压缩，可能为 LVR 的 STOP 决策训练和证据记忆保留提供可核查线索；但对象是手术视频流式应用，未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成。
